experiment: 1H-15N HSQC at 750 MHz after exchange of lambda lysozyme from H2O into 99.9% D2O (amide protection to H/D exchange)
construct_or_mutation: wild-type lambda lysozyme (R gene), 158 residues, uniformly 15N-labelled
other_conditions: ~1 mM protein in 95% H2O/5% D2O for assignment; D2O spectrum in 99.9% D2O; ~65 backbone amide peaks observed in D2O; related structures: none (X-ray structures cited, ids not given)
author_claim: About 65 backbone amides remain after H2O to D2O exchange, i.e. are protected from H/D exchange by stable hydrogen bonds or burial; the paper gives no rates and no residue list for them.
anchor: The ~65 backbone amide peaks that are observed in this spectrum correspond to amides that are protected from hydrogen/deuterium exchange as a result of stable hydrogen bonds or significant burial from solvent.
locator: Extent of assignments and data deposition (Fig. 1b); conditions: Methods and experiments, NMR spectroscopy
caveat_note: Assignment paper, not a dynamics study. A single snapshot of amide protection after buffer exchange gives no exchange rates, so it shows slow H/D exchange in the experiment window, not an absence of motion. Temperature, pH and 750 MHz field match the entry card; the BMRB accession printed in the paper is 16664 whereas the entry card lists 19127.
